summary: Configured node1 so only root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs. Installed Cronie, created opsadmin, applied a root-owned 0600 allowlist, enabled the native Cronie service, and verified persistence through reboot.
actions_performed: Set /etc/cron.allow to exactly root and opsadmin with mode 0600.
Enabled and started the native cronie OpenRC service.
Verified root and opsadmin can use crontab while nobody is denied.
Restarted node1 and verified recovery and persistent enforcement.

evidence.requirement: Only root and opsadmin may schedule cron jobs
evidence.summary: Shows the exact two-user allowlist and direct pre- and post-restart behavioral tests: root and opsadmin succeed; an unlisted user receives an explicit denial.

evidence.requirement: Cron service is correctly configured and persistent
evidence.summary: Proves Cronie is installed, its native service is running and enabled, and the policy has root ownership and mode 0600.
Captures the healthy baseline boot ID, restart acknowledgement, changed boot ID, and recovered service, policy, accounts, and effective access controls.
